title: Why do stars twinkle?
examples: Teacher, why do stars look like they are dancing?
What makes the stars twinkle when we look at them?
Is it the stars themselves that are twinkling?

explain.say: Stars seem to twinkle at night. Here is why.
The air around the Earth is always moving.
The moving air bends the light from the stars.
The light bends one way, then another. So the star seems to flicker.
You can see this above a hot road on a sunny day. Things behind the hot air seem to wobble.

draw.text: Hot air bends light from objects.

explain.say: A common mistake is to think stars blink on and off. Stars shine steadily, and the air makes them flicker.

draw.text: Stars shine steadily. The air makes them flicker.

faq.q: Do stars twinkle all the time?
faq.a: Stars twinkle more when the air is moving a lot. If the air is very still, the twinkling is much less noticeable.
asks: Why do they twinkle when it is windy?

faq.q: Is the twinkling because the stars are moving?
faq.a: No, the stars are very far away and do not move enough for us to see that way. The twinkling is caused by Earth's air.

faq.q: Does the Moon twinkle like the stars?
faq.a: The Moon does not twinkle as much as the stars do. Because it is closer, its light is steadier to our eyes.

faq.q: What is the air that bends the light called?
faq.a: It is part of Earth's atmosphere. The atmosphere is the layer of air around our planet.

faq.q: Does this happen with all lights?
faq.a: It happens with any light coming from a very far source. A light source that is close to you will not show this twinkling effect.

facts: Stars are extremely far away from Earth.
The Earth's atmosphere is made of moving air.
This moving air bends the light rays coming from stars.
This bending makes the stars appear to twinkle.

quiz.why: Moving air bends the starlight, so the stars seem to twinkle.

wrong.0: Stars shine steadily, and the air makes them flicker.
wrong.2: Stars twinkle even when the Moon is out of sight.

quiz.say: The air is very still tonight. How will the stars look?
quiz.why: Still air bends the light less, so the stars look steadier.

wrong.1: More twinkling comes from more moving air.
wrong.2: Still air makes stars easier to see, not harder.

quiz.say: Things above a hot road seem to wobble. What is bending the light?
quiz.show: 🛣️ ☀️ Wobbly view above a hot road
quiz.why: Hot, moving air bends the light, so things seem to wobble.

wrong.0: Your eyes see the wobble, but the air makes it.
wrong.1: The road stays still, and the air above it moves.
